B: Hello, hello! There we go. Martin, is it?
A: That's me. Martin. And you're Daniel. Now before we start, I saw that Spurs picture behind you, so I'm going to need you to explain yourself.
B: Ha, mate, honestly, I explain myself every weekend. To myself mostly. I've got half a season ticket, so I'm paying for the privilege of being let down.
A: Well, that's on you, that is. I'm a cricket man. Somerset. Much more civilised, you sit there all day with a flask and nobody expects you to win anything.
B: Somerset, to be fair, that's a good day out. I've done Lord's a couple of times with clients. Corporate box, which I know is cheating.
A: That's proper cheating, yeah. No, see, you want to be on a plastic seat at the County Ground in April, freezing, watching the seamers. That's cricket.
B: Ha, yeah, no, totally, I'll take that. So where are you calling from, then?
A: Taunton. Born and bred Somerset, never strayed far. Plymouth for uni, Exeter for teacher training, and then back. I was a geography teacher for, er, near enough thirty years.
B: Geography teacher, that makes sense with the map behind you. Is that Exmoor?
A: It is, well spotted. You get a gold star. Are you still teaching? No, sorry, I'm the one who was teaching. I finished a couple of years back. Bit of a, er, it wasn't really my choice in the end, the stress got me. Inspections and paperwork, all that. I do a bit of exam invigilating now at the college. Sitting in a sports hall making sure nobody's got their phone out.
B: That sounds like a decent gig, honestly. Quiet.
A: It's quiet all right. Too quiet some days. What about you, then, you look like you're in an office.
B: Yeah, I'm a solicitor. Commercial property, so leases, buying and selling buildings for investors, a couple of retail chains. I'm at a firm in the City, near Liverpool Street. Senior associate, sort of the bit before partner, which is the next step, hopefully.
A: A lawyer. I knew it. I said to myself, he's too neat and tidy, that one. No offence.
B: None taken, mate, my wife says the same. She's a physio, she thinks I iron my running kit.
A: Do you?
B: Once. Once, and I've never lived it down.
A: Ha! Good man. My Karen would never let that go either. My daughter's a bit like you, mind, organised, she's in Cardiff now. And my son's in Bristol. Proper sensible, both of them, I don't know where they got it.
B: That's nice they're not far from you, though.
A: Not far, no. Still, it's a quiet house now. Just me and the dog, Biscuit, who's mainly a sofa with ears. Anyway, how did you find that puzzle thing at the start? I thought some of those were daft, if I'm honest.
B: The puzzle, yeah. I quite enjoyed it, to be fair. I like that sort of thing, I do the pub quiz near us on a Tuesday.
A: Now you're talking. I'm the geography and sport man on our team. We lost by one point again last week. One point! On a question about the longest river in Asia, and I'd said Yangtze and got talked out of it.
B: Ah, no, that's brutal. That's the worst kind.
A: I'm still not over it. Never go against your gut, that's my lesson in life.
B: Honestly, that's how I feel about Spurs every August. I go in all optimistic and then
A: Well, there's your problem, see, you shouldn't
